themes.title: Far-right leaders face legal and political challenges
themes.blurb: Across multiple countries, far-right leaders are confronting significant legal and political hurdles. In France, Marine Le Pen's legal troubles continue as she appeals her conviction while running for president. In Poland, PiS faces internal divisions and public backlash over historical commemorations. Hungary's Fidesz is protesting constitutional changes that threaten its power.

themes.title: Right-wing parties push anti-immigration policies in Europe
themes.blurb: Anti-immigration policies are a central focus for right-wing parties across Europe. Germany's AfD proposes mandatory work for asylum seekers and stricter deportation rules. Italy's Lega and Fratelli d'Italia emphasize security and stricter immigration controls. Spain's Vox advocates for national priority in housing and social services, often targeting immigrant populations.

themes.title: Trump-Meloni feud escalates ahead of NATO summit
themes.blurb: The ongoing feud between Donald Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has intensified in the lead-up to the NATO summit. Reports highlight their strained relationship, with Trump making derogatory remarks about Meloni and her administration. This tension reflects broader transatlantic divisions within right-wing leadership.

themes.title: Milei’s ‘shutdown’ policy sparks global right-wing emulation
themes.blurb: Javier Milei's implementation of a 'shutdown' policy in Argentina has sparked interest and potential emulation among right-wing leaders globally. This policy, aimed at curbing government spending, is being closely watched by leaders in Spain, Italy, and the US, who are considering similar measures to address fiscal challenges.

themes.title: Public media crackdowns fuel far-right backlash
themes.blurb: Government crackdowns on public media are provoking strong reactions from far-right parties across Europe. In Hungary, Fidesz protests changes to state media control. In Poland, PiS criticizes media reforms and alleged bias. Germany's AfD opposes public broadcasting policies, while Spain's Vox challenges media regulations and funding.
